relevance_reason: Reports a novel hemizygous EIF2S3 variant (p.Pro432Ser) in a family with a milder phenotype in the MEHMO/EIF2S3 spectrum, with clinical, segregation, and functional data.

findings.statement: Gregory et al. (2019) described 3 affected males from a nonconsanguineous white European family: monozygotic twin brothers (III4, III5) and their maternal cousin (III3). They had severe recurrent hypoglycemia, short stature with GH and TSH deficiencies, mild learning difficulties, and an unusual form of glucose dysregulation that fluctuated between hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia and postprandial hyperglycemia. Brain MRI showed variable white matter loss and a small anterior pituitary with normal posterior pituitary and stalk. Severe intellectual disability and microcephaly were absent, and all 3 boys attended mainstream school.
quotes: Three affected males, monozygotic (identical) twin brothers (III4, III5) and their maternal cousin (III3), born to a non-consanguineous white European pedigree, presented with severe recurrent hypoglycaemia, short stature with GH and TSH deficiencies, and an unique pancreatic phenotype (Table 1).
Brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) revealed variable white matter loss and a small anterior pituitary (AP) with a normal posterior pituitary (PP) and stalk in the three boys (Fig. 1D-F).
Severe ID and microcephaly were not present in the boys, and all attend a mainstream school.

phenotypes.text: intestinal lymphonodular hyperplasia with eosinophilic infiltration

findings.statement: Gregory et al. (2019) reported that patient III3 presented with poor feeding and hypoglycemia 18 hours after birth, had total anomalous pulmonary venous return, severe gastroesophageal reflux requiring Nissen fundoplication, GH deficiency, global developmental delay needing 1:1 support, behavioral problems, and mild hepatomegaly. MRI also showed hypoplasia of the corpus callosum and ventricular asymmetry. An OGTT at 8 years showed symptomatic hypoglycemia at 3 hours with inappropriate insulin, suggesting hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia.
quotes: He presented with poor feeding and hypoglycaemia 18 h after birth. He had congenital heart disease in the form of total anomalous pulmonary venous return at presentation, as well as severe gastro-oesophageal reflux requiring Nissen fundoplication.
He has global developmental delay needing 1:1 support in mainstream school, behavioural problems and mild hepatomegaly with normal liver function.
In addition, hypoplasia of the corpus callosum and ventricular asymmetry were noted in patient III3 (Fig. 1D).

findings.statement: Gregory et al. (2019) reported that the monozygotic twins (III4, III5) had intestinal lymphonodular hyperplasia, hypoglycemic seizures and GH deficiency at 2 years, central hypothyroidism at 2 years, and microphallus that enlarged on GH therapy; III4 had transient undescended testes. They had delayed speech with mild conductive hearing loss and behavioral and mild learning difficulties. At 10 years they had impaired glucose tolerance with fluctuation between hypoglycemia and hyperglycemia, elevated HbA1c, and persisting hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia at 13.6 years; they progressed through puberty spontaneously.
quotes: Both patients presented with hypoglycaemic seizures at 2 years of age, and a diagnosis of GHD was made. Both boys had a microphallus increasing in size following commencement of GH treatment at 3.2 years of age.
By 4 years of age, the brothers had delayed speech development with mild conductive hearing loss, and behavioural and mild learning difficulties were present by the age of 6 years.
At 10 years of age, the brothers had impaired glucose tolerance upon testing; the glucose concentrations fluctuated between hypoglycaemia and hyperglycaemia (Table 2).

findings.statement: In 3 affected males of a family with hypopituitarism and glucose dysregulation, Gregory et al. (2019) identified by X-exome sequencing a hemizygous c.1294C-T transition in the EIF2S3 gene, resulting in a pro432-to-ser (P432S) substitution at a highly conserved residue in the C-terminal domain of eIF2-gamma. The variant was inherited from heterozygous mothers (sisters), originating from the heterozygous maternal grandmother, and segregated in an X-linked recessive manner over 3 generations. It was absent from ExAC and gnomAD and predicted deleterious.
quotes: sequencing of the X chromosome in Pedigree 1 revealed a novel hemizygous variant in EIF2S3 (ENST00000253039.8): ChrX_24091319 C/T, c.1294C > T, p.Pro432Ser (GRCh37) in all 3 affected males, inherited from their heterozygous mothers (sisters).

The EIF2S3 c.1294C > T, p.Pro432Ser variant was absent from control databases including the Exome Aggregation Consortium (ExAC) (www.exac.broadinstitute.org) and the Genome Aggregation Database 2018 (gnomAD) (www.gnomad.broadinstitute.org).
segregates in an X-linked recessive manner in three generations of Pedigree 1 (Fig. 2A), having been inherited from the heterozygous maternal grandmother.

findings.statement: Gregory et al. (2019) noted that the mother of the twins had secondary amenorrhea with osteoporosis, menarche at 13 years and cessation of periods at 16 years, and a normal brain MRI; the mother of III3 also presented with secondary amenorrhea.
quotes: Their mother had osteoporosis due to secondary amenorrhoea, with menarche at 13 years and cessation of periods at 16 years of age, after which she received oestrogen supplementation (CycloProgynova).
His mother presented with secondary amenorrhoea.

findings.statement: Gregory et al. (2019) screened 103 patients with congenital hypopituitarism (isolated GHD, septooptic dysplasia, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism/Kallmann syndrome, multiple pituitary hormone deficiencies) and identified no further EIF2S3 variants; none had glucose dysregulation similar to the index family.
quotes: 103 patients with variable congenital hypopituitarism phenotypes, +/− structural midline brain defects on MRI, were screened for EIF2S3 variants
No further variants were identified in these patients.

findings.statement: Gregory et al. (2019) found by in situ hybridization that EIF2S3 was expressed in the human embryonic ventral hypothalamus, Rathke's pouch, anterior and posterior pituitary, nasal epithelium progenitors and retina at Carnegie stages 20 and 23, and in the islets of Langerhans of a 13-week fetal pancreas. In a human pancreatic beta-cell line (1.1B4), shRNA knockdown of EIF2S3 by 82% caused significantly increased basal and cytokine-stimulated caspase activity, suggesting increased apoptosis.
quotes: EIF2S3 mRNA transcripts were visualised in the hypothalamus and Rathke's pouch, both the AP and PP, the progenitor cells of the nasal epithelium, and the retina of the eye at both CS20 and 23 of human development respectively
The EIF2S3 transcripts were also strongly detected in the pancreas of a 13-week old human fetus
the EIF2S3 KD cell line had significantly higher basal and cytokine-stimulated caspase activities compared to control cells (Fig. 4), suggesting increased apoptosis.

findings.statement: Gregory et al. (2019) introduced the yeast equivalent of P432S (P490S, in a locally humanized eIF2-gamma) into yeast. It did not affect growth but caused a modest (~1.7-fold) significant increase in GCN4-lacZ expression, compared with ~11-fold for the I318M equivalent of the I259M mutation, and increased UUG start codon initiation from ~1.6% to 3% of AUG. The authors concluded that P432S modestly impairs eIF2 function and may cause disease by altering the fidelity of start site selection.
quotes: The p.P490S mutation resulted in a modest, but statistically significant, ~1.7-fold increase in GCN-lacZ expression, while the I318M mutation conferred nearly an 11-fold increase in GCN4-lacZ expression.
Introduction of the P490S mutation, however, increased HIS4(UUG)-lacZ expression to 3% of the value obtained with the AUG-initiated reporter (Fig. 5E, third bar).
Cumulatively, our results demonstrate that the human p.Pro432Ser eIF2γ modestly impairs eIF2 function and may cause disease by altering the fidelity of translation start site selection.

findings.statement: Gregory et al. (2019) noted that their patients lacked the microcephaly, epilepsy and obesity that are prominent in previously reported MEHMO patients and had a much milder neurodevelopmental phenotype. They proposed that the milder loss of function of P432S produces a phenotype distinct from classic MEHMO syndrome, and suggested that untreated hypoketotic hypoglycemia may have contributed to the more severe neurodevelopmental impairment and seizures in previously reported cases.
quotes: Our patients do not have microcephaly, epilepsy, or obesity which are prominent phenotypes in previous patients diagnosed with MEHMO syndrome (Table 3).
This milder loss of function compared with previous EIF2S3 mutations, gives rise to a phenotype that is distinct from the classical spectrum of MEHMO syndrome.
It is worth considering that untreated hypoketotic hypoglycaemia in the previously published cases may have contributed to their more severe impairment of neurodevelopment and seizures.

findings.statement: Gregory et al. (2019) treated the patients with recombinant human GH, thyroxine, and diazoxide with chlorothiazide; diazoxide and chlorothiazide were stopped when hyperinsulinism resolved at 7 years, but the twins later had postprandial hyperglycemia and variable fasting hypoglycemia. The boys grew well on GH. The authors suggested that early molecular diagnosis may prevent significant morbidity and neurodevelopmental delay.
quotes: They were treated with rhGH (Fig. 1A-C), thyroxine and diazoxide together with chlorothiazide. The latter two medications were stopped as the hyperinsulinism resolved at 7 years of age; however, the twins manifested glucose dysregulation with post-prandial hyperglycaemia and variable fasting hypoglycaemia.
Early identification of such patients with a rapid molecular diagnosis may lead to prevention of significant morbidity in these patients.

relevance_reason: The paper identifies EIF2S3 mutations as the cause of MEHMO syndrome. It describes four families, the variants found, a founder effect and functional studies in yeast and patient fibroblasts.

findings.statement: Skopkova et al. (2017) described MEHMO as a rare X-linked syndrome characterized by profound intellectual disability, epilepsy, hypogonadism and hypogenitalism, microcephaly, and obesity. They linked it to mutations in EIF2S3, which encodes the gamma subunit of translation initiation factor eIF2, and placed it among disorders of translation initiation and the integrated stress response.
quotes: MEHMO is a rare X-linked syndrome characterized by profound intellectual disability, epilepsy, hypogonadism and hypogenitalism, microcephaly, and obesity.
Increased expression of DDIT3 and its corresponding protein CHOP show that MEHMO syndrome belongs to the group of disorders caused by dysregulation of translation or the UPR (Table 3).

findings.statement: Skopkova et al. (2017) reported a Slovak boy (family 1) born to nonconsanguineous parents. Microcephaly was detected prenatally, and at birth he had micropenis, cryptorchidism and peripheral hypertonia. He developed drug-resistant partial complex seizures at 4 months, severe developmental delay, central obesity, and non-autoimmune insulin-treated diabetes diagnosed at 10 months. His dysmorphic features included full cheeks, large ears, downturned corners of the mouth, epiblepharon, tapered fingers and talipes. Brain MRI showed delayed myelination that progressed with acute demyelinating changes and cerebral atrophy. Muscle biopsy showed abnormal mitochondria, and seizures and diabetes control worsened during infections. At 5 years his height was -5 SD and his head circumference -8.4 SD.
quotes: Micropenis, cryptorchidism, and peripheral hypertonia were noticed.

Diagnosis of MEHMO was made at the age of 10 months based on the microcephaly, partial complex epileptic seizures (diagnosed at the age of 4 months) resistant to anticonvulsives, hypogenitalism, severe mental and motor delay (corresponding to 3rd month of life)

Brain MRI at the age of 4 months showed mild myelination delay corresponding to 2nd-3rd month, and the myelination delay was more pronounced at the age of 19 months with further acute demyelinating changes and cerebral atrophy (Figure 1C).

findings.statement: Skopkova et al. (2017) measured respiratory chain activity in permeabilized muscle fibers from the family 1 proband. Complex II activity was reduced (1.22 vs 3.11 nM/min/mg in controls; P = 0.009), and complex IV activity was normal.
quotes: Measurements of activities of respiratory chain complexes II and IV in patient 1 muscle (Table 2) showed decreased complex II and normal complex IV activities.

phenotypes.text: decreased complex II activity in muscle
phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex II

findings.statement: Skopkova et al. (2017) reported a second Slovak boy (family 2) from a nonconsanguineous family, with an unaffected mother and no other affected relatives. He had a birth head circumference of -5.1 SD, therapy-resistant seizures from 6 months without an EEG correlate, hypogenitalism, severe developmental delay, central obesity, and dysmorphic features. He had non-autoimmune insulin-treated diabetes from 10 months, and MRI showed delayed myelination. At 3 years he was hypotonic, had no voluntary movements and showed no social interaction.
quotes: MEHMO features included microcephaly, therapy resistant seizures (diagnosed at the age of 6 months) without EEG correlation, hypogenitalism, severe mental and motor delay (corresponding to 3rd month of life at the age of 2 years), central obesity, and dysmorphic features very similar to the proband of family 1.
He has non-autoimmune diabetes melitus treated with insulin from 10 months.
He is hypotonic, with no voluntary movements and he does not show any social interaction.

findings.statement: Skopkova et al. (2017) restudied the German family originally reported by Steinmüller et al. The index patient was diagnosed with microcephaly prenatally and was born at 32 weeks. He had therapy-resistant seizures from 7 weeks, hypogenitalism, severe delay and central obesity. His dysmorphic features included facial telangiectasias, edematous hands and feet, and bilateral talipes. Diabetes was diagnosed at 6 months after a ketoacidotic crisis, and he died at 2 years with refractory seizures. Female carriers in the family were unaffected.
quotes: MEHMO features included microcephaly, therapy resistant epileptic seizures (diagnosed at the age of 7 weeks), hypogenitalism, severe mental and motor delay, central obesity, and dysmorphic features including narrow forehead, full cheeks, facial telangiectasias, downturned corners of the mouth, large ears, edematous hands and feet, tapered fingers, and bilateral talipes.
Diabetes was diagnosed at age of 6 months due to a ketoacidotic crisis.
All females from this family who carry the EIF2S3 mutation on one of their X chromosomes were unaffected.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Edema of the dorsum of hands

findings.statement: Skopkova et al. (2017) reported a boy (family 4) of Northern European origin living in the US, born to nonconsanguineous parents. He had microcephaly, hypospadias, cryptorchidism, developmental delay, and obesity that followed a period of failure to thrive. He had no epileptic seizures and his EEG was normal. He also had hypotonia with peripheral spasticity, chronic lung disease, dysphagia, delayed gastric emptying, grade 5 vesicoureteral reflux and congenital scoliosis, but no diabetes.
quotes: MEHMO features included microcephaly, hypospadia and cryptorchidism, developmental delay, and obesity with BMI at the 97th centile (after a longer period of failure to thrive). He does not have epileptic seizures and his EEG was normal.
He has central hypotonia and peripheral hypertonia and spasticity, chronic lung disease, dysphagia, delayed gastric emptying, and grade 5 vesico-ureteral reflux (Table 1).

findings.statement: In affected males from 3 families with MEHMO syndrome (2 Slovak families and the German family originally reported by Steinmüller et al.), Skopkova et al. (2017) used whole-exome or X-chromosome exome sequencing to identify the same hemizygous 4-bp deletion in the last exon of EIF2S3 (c.1394_1397delTCAA). The deletion causes a frameshift (p.Ile465Serfs*4) that replaces the last 8 amino acids with 3 different ones. It segregated with the disease, was absent from dbSNP and ExAC, and had a CADD score of 35.
quotes: Strikingly, families 1, 2 and 3 carried the identical 4 bp deletion c.1394_1397delTCAA, which co-segregated with the disease in the families and is predicted to cause a frameshift and a premature stop codon (p.Ile465Serfs*4) in the EIF2S3 encoded protein eIF2γ.
The mutations were not present in public databases, including dbSNP147 (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/SNP/), and ExAC (http://exac.broadinstitute.org).

findings.statement: In the boy from family 4, who had a milder phenotype, Skopkova et al. (2017) identified by trio exome sequencing a hemizygous missense variant in EIF2S3 (c.324T>A, p.Ser108Arg) that he inherited from his healthy mother. The variant changes a serine that is conserved down to Drosophila, was absent from dbSNP and ExAC, and had a CADD score of 24. The equivalent yeast mutation (Asp167Arg) had no effect, and the healthy brother could not be tested, so the authors classified the variant as of unknown significance.
quotes: The patient from family 4 carried a point mutation, c.324T>A, which he inherited from his healthy mother (Figure 1A) and could not be tested in his healthy brother.

Combining the results obtained in yeast with the limited number of family members tested for the variant, we currently interprete the p.Ser108Arg substitution as a variant of unknown significance according to American College of Medical Genetics guidelines.

findings.statement: The 3 families carrying c.1394_1397delTCAA reported no common ancestors, and identity-by-descent analysis excluded relationships closer than about fourth-degree cousins. However, Skopkova et al. (2017) found that comparison of sequencing data and haplotypes suggested a founder effect with more distant relatedness.
quotes: Subsequent comparison of WES data from index patients of the Slovak families 1 and 2, the mother from family 2, and X-chromosome sequencing data from the index patient from family 3 suggested a founder effect in these three families but with more distant relatedness (Supp. Tables S1 and S2).

findings.statement: Skopkova et al. (2017) found no EIF2S3 coding variants in the 2 previously reported MEHMO families (DeLozier-Blanchet et al. and Leshinsky-Silver et al.). The Leshinsky-Silver patient carried a SERAC1 p.Tyr430X mutation. The authors suggested that in the DeLozier-Blanchet family the defect could lie outside the regions covered by exome sequencing, or in another gene that mimics MEHMO.
quotes: In two families, no mutation was found in the EIF2S3 gene.

While the patient reported by Leshinsky-Silver et al carried a deleterious (p.Tyr430X) mutation in the SERAC1 (MIM# 614725) gene, the genetic defect in the family reported by DeLozier-Blanchet could be located outside the EIF2S3 region examined by WES or the disease in this family might have been caused by a mutation in another gene mimicking the MEHMO syndrome.

findings.statement: Skopkova et al. (2017) built a yeast/human eIF2-gamma chimera to model the variant. The chimera carrying Ile465Serfs*4 caused slow growth that was worse at 37 degrees C, and it was expressed at normal protein levels. It derepressed GCN4-lacZ expression nearly 3-fold and doubled the UUG/AUG initiation ratio, effects comparable to the XLID-associated Val281Thr mutation. These results indicated that the C-terminal mutation impairs eIF2 function.
quotes: In contrast, yeast expressing the Sc/Hs-Ile465Serfs*4 mutant exhibited a slight slow growth (Slg-) phenotype at 30 °C that was exacerbated at 37 °C (Figure 3C).

Whereas GCN4-lacZ reporter expression was similarly repressed in yeast expressing wild type eIF2γ or the Sc/Hs chimera, the Ile465Serfs*4 mutation derepressed GCN4 expression nearly 3-fold, comparably to cells expressing eIF2γ-Val281Thr (Figure 4A).

Consistent with the notion that the eIF2γ-Ile465Serfs*4 mutation impairs eIF2 function, the UUG/AUG ratio was increased ~2-fold in cells expressing this eIF2γ mutant compared to cells expressing the Sc/Hs chimera (Figure 4B, 2nd and 3rd bar).

findings.statement: In patient fibroblasts, Skopkova et al. (2017) showed that the C-terminally truncated eIF2-gamma protein is produced. In fibroblasts from a family 3 patient with Ile465Serfs*4, DDIT3 transcript levels were 2.5-fold higher than in controls and CHOP protein was also elevated. This indicated activation of the integrated stress response.
quotes: These results demonstrate that eIF2γ is expressed in human fibroblasts as expected given its essential role in cellular protein synthesis, and that the C-terminal truncated protein is produced in the patients.

The DDIT3 transcript level was significantly increased (2.5-fold) in the patient relative to the controls (Figure 5A), and Western blot analysis of whole cell lysates confirmed significantly elevated CHOP protein levels in the patient compared to control fibroblasts

findings.statement: Skopkova et al. (2017) noted that all 4 index patients with the C-terminal frameshift mutation (including a previously reported family) had full MEHMO syndrome. Three of them developed insulin-dependent diabetes in the first year, and none achieved head control, voluntary movement or social interaction. Patients with missense mutations (p.Ser108Arg, p.Ile259Met, p.Ile222Thr) were less severely affected and had only subsets of the features. The authors proposed that more severe EIF2S3 mutations cause full MEHMO and less deleterious ones cause a milder form.
quotes: All four index patients carrying the C-terminal frameshift mutation presented the full spectrum of MEHMO syndrome including microcephaly, epileptic seizures, hypogonadism, hypogenitalism, and obesity. Moreover, three of the patients developed insulin-dependent diabetes in the first year of life.

In contrast, the patients with the missense mutations identified to date are less severely affected and present only subsets of symptoms that can differ even within family members carrying the same mutation.
Thus, we propose that more severe EIF2S3 mutations cause the full MEHMO phenotype, while less deleterious mutations cause a milder form of the syndrome with only a subset of the symptoms.

findings.statement: Skopkova et al. (2017) proposed that EIF2S3 mutations, like mutations in the EIF2B genes and PPP1R15B, reduce the activity or availability of the eIF2 ternary complex. They suggested this leads to insufficient protein synthesis and chronically elevated ATF4 and CHOP, causing apoptosis. They also noted that, as in vanishing white matter disease, patient 1's condition worsened markedly during illness.
quotes: Mutations in eIF2γ, like mutations in EIF2B1 (MIM# 606686), EIF2B2 (MIM# 606454), EIF2B3 (MIM# 606273), EIF2B4 (MIM# 606687), EIF2B5 (MIM# 603945), and PPP1R15B (MIM# 613257), impair the activity or availability of TC.
Moreover, the decreased translation rate and attendant chronically elevated ATF4 and CHOP levels result in apoptosis.
Like the VWM patients, the condition of Patient 1 in our study was markedly aggravated during periods of illness.

relevance_reason: Reports two families with EIF2S3 mutations causing syndromic X-linked intellectual disability (MEHMO spectrum), with zebrafish functional support.

findings.statement: Moortgat et al. (2016) described 2 unrelated families with suspected X-linked syndromic intellectual disability in which affected males had severe intellectual disability, microcephaly, growth retardation, and epilepsy.
quotes: X-chromosome exome sequencing was performed to identify the genetic cause of syndromic intellectual disability in two unrelated families with suspected X-linked inheritance.
In both families, affected males presented with severe intellectual disability, microcephaly, growth retardation, and epilepsy.

findings.statement: In affected males from one of 2 families with syndromic X-linked intellectual disability, Moortgat et al. (2016) identified by X-chromosome exome sequencing a hemizygous missense mutation in the EIF2S3 gene, c.777T>G (p.Ile259Met); obligate carrier females were heterozygous.
quotes: A missense mutation (c.777T>G p.(Ile259Met)) and a frameshift mutation (c.1394_1397del p.(Ile465Serfs*4)) were identified in the EIF2S3 gene in the hemizygous state in affected patients, and in the heterozygous states female obligate carriers.

findings.statement: In affected males from the second family with syndromic X-linked intellectual disability, Moortgat et al. (2016) identified a hemizygous frameshift mutation in the EIF2S3 gene, c.1394_1397del (p.Ile465SerfsTer4); obligate carrier females were heterozygous.
quotes: A missense mutation (c.777T>G p.(Ile259Met)) and a frameshift mutation (c.1394_1397del p.(Ile465Serfs*4)) were identified in the EIF2S3 gene in the hemizygous state in affected patients, and in the heterozygous states female obligate carriers.

findings.statement: Moortgat et al. (2016) found that morpholino-based knockdown of the zebrafish EIF2S3 ortholog (eif2s3) recapitulated the human microcephaly and short stature phenotype, supporting pathogenicity of the identified variants.
quotes: Morpholino-based knockdown of the zebrafish EIF2S3 ortholog (eif2s3) recapitulates the human microcephaly and short stature phenotype, supporting the pathogenicity of the identified variants.

relevance_reason: Reports the original family with X-linked ID/microcephaly caused by EIF2S3 p.Ile222Thr, the Borck-type XLID now within the MEHMO spectrum, with functional studies.

findings.statement: Borck et al. (2012) described a family of Moroccan Jewish ancestry in the maternal line in which 3 males had an X-linked intellectual disability syndrome with moderate-to-severe ID, microcephaly, short stature, and facial dysmorphism. Individual features included cleft lip and palate and behavioral impairment (III:1), generalized seizures (III:2), and postpubertal microgenitalism and obesity (II:3). Brain MRI showed a thin corpus callosum and enlarged lateral ventricles. The parents I.1 and I.2 were first cousins.
quotes: We ascertained a family of Morocco Jewish ancestry in the maternal line in which three male individuals were affected by an intellectual disability (ID) syndrome with apparent X-chromosomal inheritance (X-linked ID, XLID) (Figure 1A). Clinical features included moderate-to-severe ID, microcephaly, short stature, and facial dysmorphic features (Figure S1).

Additionally, each of the affected individuals had unique symptoms including cleft lip and palate and behavioral impairments (individual III:1), generalized seizures (III:2), and postpubertal microgenitalism and obesity (II:3) (see Supplemental Data). Brain magnetic resonance imaging revealed a thin corpus callosum and enlarged lateral ventricles (Figure 1B).
the double line connecting I.1 and I.2 indicates consanguinity (I.1 and I.2 are first cousins)

findings.statement: By targeted linkage analysis using 18 X-chromosomal STR markers in 10 family members, Borck et al. (2012) identified a 10.7-Mb candidate region at Xp22.11-p21.1 containing 35 annotated genes.
quotes: Targeted linkage analysis was performed and a candidate region spanning 10.7 megabases on the short arm of the X chromosome (Xp22.11-p21.1; Figure S2A) and containing 35 annotated genes (Figure S2B) was identified.

findings.statement: In the 3 affected males of a Moroccan Jewish family with XLID and microcephaly, Borck et al. (2012) identified a hemizygous c.665T>C (p.Ile222Thr) missense mutation in the EIF2S3 gene by exome sequencing within the linkage region, confirmed by Sanger sequencing. The mutation cosegregated with the disorder, female carriers were heterozygous, and it was absent from 188 Moroccan Jewish control X chromosomes, dbSNP132, 1000 Genomes, and >8,000 ESP alleles. Ile222 lies in the GTP-binding domain and is strictly conserved in animals.
quotes: Capillary sequencing confirmed the c.665T>C (p.Ile222>Thr) mutation (Figure 1C) and showed that it cosegregated with the ID syndrome in the family.

This variant was not detected in 188 X chromosomes from Morocco Jewish controls, nor was it present in dbSNP132, the 1000 Genomes data, or >8,000 alleles sequenced by the NHLBI Exome Sequencing Project.
Ile222 is located in the GTP-binding (G) domain of eIF2γ (Figure 1D) and is strictly conserved in the animal kingdom

findings.statement: Borck et al. (2012) found no additional EIF2S3 mutations by sequencing all 12 exons in 60 individuals from families with unspecific, potentially X-linked ID, suggesting that EIF2S3 mutations confer a specific phenotype.
quotes: we did not identify additional mutations in 60 affected individuals from families with unspecific (and potentially X-linked) ID by sequencing the 12 EIF2S3 exons
suggests that EIF2S3 mutations confer a specific phenotype

findings.statement: Borck et al. (2012) noted a previously reported EIF2S3 missense variant c.451G>C (p.V151L) from an XLID resequencing project, absent from SNP databases and predicted damaging; the orthologous yeast V210L mutation, near the Met-tRNAi binding site, caused defects in growth, GCN4 expression, and start site selection, and the growth defect was suppressed by tRNAi(Met) overexpression, suggesting impaired Met-tRNAi binding.
quotes: We noted that a distinct missense variant (c.451G>C, p.V151L) was previously reported by a large-scale resequencing project of X-chromosomal genes in families with XLID.

our analysis of the orthologous V210L mutation that lies near the Met-tRNAi Met binding site in yeast eIF2γ (Figure S4A) revealed defects in cell growth, GCN4 expression and translation start site selection (Figure S4B–C).

findings.statement: Borck et al. (2012) found that myc/His6-tagged human eIF2-gamma I222T expressed in HeLa cells pulled down substantially less endogenous eIF2-beta than wildtype, without affecting eIF2-alpha binding, indicating disrupted eIF2 complex integrity. Structural modeling on archaeal aIF2 placed the corresponding residue in the hydrophobic cleft binding eIF2-beta helix alpha-1.
quotes: Whereas eIF2α and eIF2β were co-precipitated with the tagged wild type eIF2γ on Ni2+ affinity resin (Figure 2E, lanes 3–4), substantially less eIF2β was pulled-down with eIF2γ-I222T (Figure 2E, lanes 5–6).
the I222T mutation identified in the affected individuals disrupts eIF2 complex formation by specifically impairing the binding of eIF2β to human eIF2γ.

findings.statement: Borck et al. (2012) found that yeast eIF2-gamma with the analogous V281T mutation impaired eIF2-beta binding without affecting growth, whereas V281K nearly abolished eIF2-beta binding and impaired growth. Both mutations increased GCN4-lacZ expression (2.5- and 40-fold) and raised the UUG/AUG initiation ratio 2-3-fold; eIF2-beta overexpression partially suppressed these defects. The authors concluded that the mutation impairs eIF2 integrity, ternary complex function, and start codon fidelity.
quotes: In contrast, the eIF2γ-V281T mutation substantially impaired eIF2β binding (Figure 2D, lanes 5–6), indicating that a substantial loss of eIF2 integrity is tolerated in yeast without an affect on cell growth.
The V281T and V281K mutations in eIF2γ increased expression of a GCN4-lacZ reporter 2.5- and 40-fold, respectively (Table 1, panel A).
The V281T and V281K mutations in eIF2γ increased the UUG/AUG initiation ratio by 2–3 fold (Table 1, panel B).

relevance_reason: Case report of a child with MEHMO syndrome showing mitochondrial respiratory chain dysfunction, the first evidence that MEHMO is a mitochondrial disorder.

findings.statement: Leshinsky-Silver et al. (2002) described a child with MEHMO syndrome (mental retardation, epileptic seizures, hypogenitalism, microcephaly, and obesity) who also had lactic acidosis. Histologic staining of a muscle biopsy showed mitochondrial proliferation and lipid storage. Electron microscopy showed abnormal, enlarged mitochondria with concentric cristae and electron-dense bodies.
quotes: We describe a child with MEHMO and lactic acidosis whose muscle biopsy revealed markedly reduced activities of complexes 1,3 and 4 of the mitochondrial electron transport chain.
Histological staining showed mitochondrial proliferation and lipid storage. Electron microscopy revealed abnormal and enlarged mitochondria with concentric cristae and electron dense bodies.

phenotypes.text: abnormal enlarged mitochondria with concentric cristae

findings.statement: Leshinsky-Silver et al. (2002) found markedly reduced activities of complexes I, III, and IV of the mitochondrial electron transport chain in a muscle biopsy from a child with MEHMO syndrome. They concluded that this was the first identification of MEHMO as a mitochondrial disorder, and one of the very few X-linked mitochondrial syndromes.
quotes: We describe a child with MEHMO and lactic acidosis whose muscle biopsy revealed markedly reduced activities of complexes 1,3 and 4 of the mitochondrial electron transport chain.
This is the first identification of MEHMO as a mitochondrial disorder and one of the very few X-linked mitochondrial syndromes.

phenotypes.text: decreased activity of mitochondrial complex I
phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex I

phenotypes.text: decreased activity of mitochondrial complex III
phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased activity of mitochondrial complex III

phenotypes.text: decreased activity of mitochondrial complex IV

relevance_reason: The title reports that the MEHMO syndrome locus was assigned to Xp21.1-p22.13, which is the subject of this entry.

findings.statement: DeLozier-Blanchet et al. (1999) assigned the disease locus for MEHMO syndrome to chromosome Xp21.1-p22.13.
quotes: MEHMO, a novel syndrome: assignment of disease locus to Xp21.1-p22.13.

findings.statement: DeLozier-Blanchet et al. (1999) described MEHMO as a new syndrome made up of mental retardation, epileptic seizures, hypogonadism and hypogenitalism, microcephaly, and obesity.
quotes: Mental retardation, epileptic seizures, hypogonadism and genitalism, microcephaly, obesity.

relevance_reason: Original description of MEHMO syndrome and mapping of its locus to Xp21.1-p22.13.

findings.statement: Steinmüller et al. (1998) described a previously unrecognized X-linked mental retardation syndrome in a large 3-generation family, with clinical hallmarks of mental retardation, epileptic seizures, hypogonadism and hypogenitalism, microcephaly, and obesity. Patients had a life expectancy of less than 2 years.
quotes: A previously unrecognised X-chromosomal mental retardation syndrome is described. Clinical hallmarks are mental retardation, epileptic seizures, hypogonadism, and -genitalism, microcephaly and obesity. Life expectancy of patients is less than two years.

findings.statement: Steinmüller et al. (1998) designated the condition by the acronym MEHMO, based on its major clinical features: mental retardation, epileptic seizures, hypogonadism and hypogenitalism, microcephaly, and obesity.
quotes: Based on the major clinical symptoms this condition is referred to by the acronym MEHMO.

findings.statement: By haplotype and 2-point linkage analyses in a large 3-generation family, Steinmüller et al. (1998) mapped the MEHMO disease locus to Xp21.1-p22.13, in a region flanked by CYBB and DXS365.
quotes: Haplotype and two-point linkage analyses in a large three-generation family assign the disease locus to Xp21.1-p22.13, to a region that is flanked by CYBB and DXS365.

relevance_reason: The paper gives the original clinical description of two brothers with severe microcephaly, growth and mental retardation, obesity, hypogonadism and neurological abnormalities, which matches the MEHMO phenotype. The authors propose recessive inheritance, probably X-linked.

findings.statement: Delozier-Blanchet et al. (1989) described 2 brothers with severe postnatal growth retardation and severe mental retardation, extreme microcephaly, obesity developing during infancy, microgonadism, and a characteristic amphora-shaped facies. Neurologic examination showed hypertonia, hyperreflexia, nystagmus, and extremely irritable and agitated behavior. The first child died at 4.5 years and had also had neonatal hypoglycemia and chronic constipation.
quotes: Two brothers are described with a severe syndrome of postnatal growth and mental retardation which includes extreme microcephaly, obesity developing during infancy, microgonadismsm, and a characteristic amphora-shaped facies.
The neurological exam is highly abnormal, with hypertonia and hyperreflexia, nystagmus, and an extremely irritable and agitated behavior.
The first child, who died at 4/1/2 years, also presented neonatal hypoglycemia and chronic constipation.

findings.statement: Delozier-Blanchet et al. (1989) noted that the cause was unknown. They suggested recessive inheritance, either autosomal or X-linked, and considered an X-linked recessive gene especially tempting because of the importance of the X chromosome in mental retardation.
quotes: Although the etiology of this syndrome is unknown, it is tempting to consider an X-linked recessive gene, given the importance of the X chromosome in mental retardation.
the etiology of which would probably be recessive, either autosomal or X-linked.

findings.statement: Delozier-Blanchet et al. (1989) found that the brothers most resembled patients with Borjeson-Forssman-Lehmann syndrome. However, their dwarfism and mental retardation were much more severe than in any reported BFL patient, and their neurologic and dysmorphic features differed significantly. The authors considered either a particularly severe, possibly allelic, variant of BFL or a previously undescribed disorder.
quotes: Among the over 70 syndromes of X-linked mental retardation already described, our patients resemble individuals with the Börjeson-Forssman-Lehmann (BFL) syndrome the most.

However, the severity of their dwarfism and mental retardation is much greater than described in any BFL patient to date, and the neurological and dysmorphic features vary significantly from those described in the BFL.
Although a particularly severe variant, perhaps allelic, is a possibility, an as yet undescribed disorder is also plausible
